cards.html: This branch is the full text of CI/CD for ML Engineers (Edition November 2026), split into 20 skills. The companion code lives in cicd-tutorial/code/credit-api and cicd-tutorial/code/rag-api.

This book takes you from "I have heard of CI/CD" to "I can build and explain a production-grade ML pipeline". It is written for a data scientist or ML engineer who knows Python and basic Git, and who wants to be fluent in delivery engineering for job interviews and real work in Germany.

Work through it with a keyboard. Every level contains hands-on tasks, complete files and exercises. The listings come from two companion projects, credit-api and rag-api, and were run before printing: the unit tests pass, the linters are clean and the evaluation gates were executed. The Git labs and most "what if" scenarios were run too. Two things could not be executed while writing: GitHub Actions runs and AWS calls. Those files were checked against the current documentation (November 2026) and parsed as valid YAML/JSON, but you will be the first to run them. That makes it a good exercise: when something is off, Appendix F lists the usual error messages and fixes.

The callout boxes

Concept

Explains an idea or term before you use it. Read these even when you skim.

Try it

A hands-on step for your machine, usually 2 to 10 minutes.

Watch out

A common mistake, a security risk, or something that costs money.

Interview tip

Sentences you can say in an interview, phrased the way an experienced engineer would.

What if… something goes wrong?

A situation you will meet at work, what happens, why, and what you do. Terminal output in these boxes is real unless it involves GitHub or AWS. Appendix A indexes them all.

Checkpoint: You should now be able to…

The end of every level: a list of skills to tick off before you move on.

Conventions

• Grey boxes: terminal (what you type; # starts a comment), expected output, or a file listing with its path in the title bar (longer files have line numbers).
  • German terms you will hear at work are added in italics, e.g. continuous delivery (kontinuierliche Bereitstellung). The glossary in Appendix G collects them.
  • Version numbers are the current ones as of November 2026. Where something is likely to change (prices, action versions), the text says so.
